intro: Anthropic's Opus 5.5 lands as the new default in Claude Code a day after OpenAI countered with cheaper GPT-6 Sol and Luna, while bitcoin's rally gets an institutional stamp from a record ETF inflow day.

items.headline: Anthropic Ships Claude Opus 5.5, Now the Default Model in Claude Code
items.summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5, the first model in its 5.5 family, cutting typical workload costs by about 40% versus Opus 5 while boosting output speed over 30%. It's now the default model in Claude Code with a 1M-token context window; an early tester used it to audit and fix a 200,000-line codebase in under three hours, versus over 20 hours for Opus 5.
items.why: A sharp jump in cost and speed changes the economics of long-running coding agents, not just their benchmark scores.

items.headline: OpenAI Launches GPT-6 Sol and Luna, Roughly Halving API Prices
items.summary: OpenAI expanded its GPT-6 family with Sol, built for coding and agentic tasks, and Luna, a lightweight model for high-volume clerical work, cutting API prices by about half versus their GPT-5.6 predecessors. Both are rolling out now in Codex, the API, and ChatGPT, with OpenAI claiming Sol makes about half as many mistakes as its predecessor at Astra-level reliability.
items.why: A coding-tuned model at half the price directly undercuts rivals' agentic-coding pricing a day after Anthropic's own cost cut.

items.headline: Amodei and Altman Set to Brief UN Security Council on AI Risks
items.summary: Anthropic's Dario Amodei and OpenAI's Sam Altman are scheduled to address the UN Security Council on AI on Wednesday, alongside Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue and AI-safety researcher Yoshua Bengio, in a session covering the risks posed by advancing AI systems.
items.why: A rare joint appearance by rival lab CEOs before the Security Council signals AI safety is now treated as international security policy, not just industry self-regulation.

items.headline: OpenAI Forms Math Advisory Group After Model Resolves 100+ Open Problems
items.summary: OpenAI said an internal model has resolved more than 100 previously open problems across mathematics and formed an independent nine-mathematician Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence, hosted at Princeton's Institute for Advanced Study, to vet and help communicate the results.
items.why: A concrete, third-party-checked claim of new math results is a higher bar than the usual benchmark-score announcement.

items.headline: GitHub's Refreshed Pull Requests Page Reaches General Availability
items.summary: GitHub shipped its redesigned repository-level pull requests page to all users, adding advanced AND/OR search, a compact presentation mode, and bulk actions like closing, labeling, and changing milestones across multiple pull requests at once.
items.why: A daily-use surface for most teams; better filtering and bulk actions cut real review overhead.

items.headline: Chrome 154 Ships Under Google's New Two-Week Release Cadence
items.summary: Google released Chrome 154 to stable on September 22, the second release under its new two-week major-version cycle, down from four weeks, which began with Chrome 153 on September 8. Extended Stable keeps its slower eight-week cycle for enterprises that need longer testing windows.
items.why: Faster browser releases shrink the lag between a web-platform feature shipping and it being safe to rely on in production.

items.headline: Spot Bitcoin ETFs Pull In Nearly $1 Billion in a Single Day
items.summary: U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs attracted $998.95 million in net inflows on Monday, the largest single-day haul in nearly a year and the ninth-largest since the funds launched, led by BlackRock's IBIT with $381.37 million. Bitcoin briefly touched about $87,300 the same day, its highest level since January.
items.why: Confirms the current rally is backed by real institutional buying rather than just leverage and spot-market momentum.

items.headline: Regulators Race to Write Crypto Rules After Clarity Act Stalls in Senate
items.summary: With the Clarity Act's comprehensive crypto framework stuck after a failed Senate procedural vote, the SEC and CFTC are moving under their existing authority to fill the gap, including an SEC 'innovation exemption' for tokenized-securities trading and a CFTC crypto rulemaking sent to the White House for review.
items.why: Sets the near-term rulebook bitcoin exchanges, custodians, and issuers will operate under while Congress remains stalled.
